title: Org admin delegation, invite compliance playbook and RBAC v2 audit schema
creator: Anika Patel
description: Design and implement a combined playbook and engineering workstream to: 1) enable org-level delegated admin and time-limited elevated roles under RBAC v2; 2) enforce invite compliance via configurable allowlist/denylist + SSO domain verification; and 3) expand audit logging schema so invite and admin events capture pre/post state and effective permissions for incident triage and compliance audits.
updates: 2025-02-12: Ticket created after security guild sync; high-level scope approved by PM + Security.
2025-02-14: Spike completed on RBAC v2 token shape and temporal approval flow; prototype repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rbac-spikes/pull/27
2025-02-16: Confluence playbook draft posted: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/Sec/Invite+Compliance+Playbook (internal); added acceptance criteria.

2025-02-18: Backend schema PR opened for audit event changes: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4123 — initial review comments from @suzanne and @lee; adjusted event naming and included 'effective_roles' field.
2025-02-19: Integration test harness updated to simulate SSO-enforced org joins; failing case found for legacy invites without domain mapping — added migration task.
2025-02-20: Design review with DX completed; console UI for admin delegation mockups linked in attachments; preparing canary rollout for 10 beta orgs.
acceptance_criteria: RBAC v2 supports time-limited delegated admin roles with auditable grant/expiry events and can be revoked via API.
Invite flow applies org-level allowlist/denylist and domain verification rules; SSO-enforced orgs reject non-compliant invites with clear error codes.

Audit log schema includes actor, actor_auth_method (api_key|sso|token), effective_roles, resource_before_snapshot_id, resource_after_snapshot_id, and human_reason; logs are queryable in Console within 30s of generation.
Migration path for existing team invites validated: legacy invites flagged and either migrated to new policy or expired based on policy window.
End-to-end tests for key scenarios (delegated admin grant, invite denylist hit, domain-verified SSO join) pass in CI with 95%+ reliability over 100 runs.
Rollout to 10 pilot orgs completed with monitoring showing no >5% increase in failed joins or >1% increased latency on invite API.
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Feature flags and internal-only endpoints (QA) — enable RBAC v2 hooks and new audit schema behind feature flag.
Phase 1: Beta with 10 pilot orgs — enable invite compliance + delegated admin for pilot orgs, monitor metrics for 2 weeks.
Phase 2: Gradual enablement by org size/region with automatic fallback to legacy invites for orgs that opt-out within 72 hours.
Phase 3: Default-on for new orgs and enforcement window for existing orgs with migration notice and admin migration tool.
Rollback: API-level feature flag to restore legacy invite semantics and an automatic retry queue for in-flight invites.
test_plan: Unit tests for audit event serializer and deserializer covering pre/post snapshots and effective_roles mapping.
Integration tests for SSO domain-verified join flow with mocked identity provider and domain-attestation service.
Chaos test: simulate invite flood and reputation service latency to validate invite throttling and graceful degradation.
Security review: run static + dynamic analysis and threat-model focused review against attack vectors (phishing invites, token replay, privilege escalation).
Load test: 10k concurrent invite attempts across multiple orgs to measure invite API latency and RBAC evaluation time.
notes: Trade-off: capturing full resource snapshots increases log size ~2.3x; chosen compromise is to store snapshot references with selective fields for sensitive resources.
Open risk: identity provider (IdP) metadata mismatch during migration — mitigation: allow manual domain-to-IdP mapping and a one-click retry in Console.
Decision: use Temporal for the approval workflow to get durable history and automatic expiry; this requires dependency ENG-95421 (temporal infra hardening).
Follow-up: propose analytics alert for sudden spike in 'invite_rejected_due_to_domain' to surface SSO config regressions.
